understanding.json.goal: Reduce the source's diagnostic maximum-rank summed NCCL kernel duration for the accumulated training step, retaining its step-time constraint and full correctness checks.
understanding.json.completion: run() executes exactly the source's timed step(): optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) first (inside the timed invocation, as the first statement of source accumulate()), then all accumulation_steps forward/backward microbatches of token ids shaped (micro_batch, sequence_length) with each microbatch's mean CE loss divided by accumulation_steps, the first accumulation_steps-1 microbatches under model.no_sync() and the final microbatch performing the DDP gradient allreduce over NCCL, followed by optimizer.step() (SGD lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0) and torch.cuda.synchronize(); that synchronize is the source's completion point and ends the measured invocation. For the frozen request this is 4 microbatches of (1, 128) per rank, effective batch 8, 1024 tokens per step. Everything else in the source is outside the workload: model/reference construction, the rank-0 serial reference and all correctness checks (global-batch gradient check, +1 negative control, exact cross-rank gradient replica broadcast, parameter update check), the bucket inventory comm hook, the 3 separate profile_once NCCL diagnostics, and result/report writing. The communication objective (communication_kernel_sum_ms, max across ranks then median of the profiled repeats) is collected by the framework's torch_communication collector in separate diagnostic runs, so metrics() reports only the source's clean step metrics.

it refuses a world size different from workload['world_size']. state = {device, rank, world_size, workload, raw_model, model (DDP), optimizer, inputs, initial, control, parameter_count, mode}. reset(state) reproduces the source's reset(): raw_model.load_state_dict(initial) from the CPU snapshot; SGD carries no momentum buffers, the step consumes no RNG (pregenerated inputs, dropout disabled), gradients are recreated by zero_grad(set_to_none=True) at the start of the timed accumulate, DDP reducer/bucket state is left as the source leaves it across repeats, and the process group is never destroyed. run(state) returns {'loss': accumulated loss tensor}; observe(state, result) returns {'loss', 'gradients': every named .grad, 'parameters': every named updated parameter} as detached CPU tensors (CPU copies so correctness capture does not inflate the CUDA peak-allocated statistic); metrics(state, result, elapsed_ms) returns step_ms, tokens_per_second = tokens_per_step*1000/step_ms, peak_allocated_bytes (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() queried outside the timer), effective_batch, tokens_per_step and parameter_count, with no fabricated communication objective. models(state) exposes {'model': raw_model} for automatic discovery and controlled replacement. set_mode() only records the mode (execution semantics and work amount are identical in quality/measure/profile); before_run() performs the source's gloo control-group barrier outside the timer. The worker-initialized process group is used as-is; no second default group is created and no CUDA work happens at import time.
invariants: Workload shape is frozen by request['workload'] (accumulated_step: world_size 2, micro_batch 1, sequence_length 128, accumulation_steps 4; effective batch 8, 1024 tokens per step): each run() must perform every microbatch's forward/backward plus exactly one optimizer update (request notes 'One measured invocation'); the adapter reads these dimensions from request['workload'] rather than embedding constants.

Gradient reference fidelity (source checks['global_batch_gradient_check'] with workloads.json correctness tolerances): the step's full gradients must match a serial single-process pass over the same seeded global batch (all ranks' inputs) within grad_atol=1e-6 and grad_rtol=1e-4.

Cross-rank gradient exactness (source checks['exact_gradient_replica_check'], torch.testing.assert_close atol=0.0, rtol=0.0): after the step's gradient synchronization every rank's full gradients must be bit-identical to every other rank's.

Parameter-update fidelity (source checks['parameter_update_check']): updated parameters must match the reference SGD update within parameter_atol=1e-6 and parameter_rtol=1e-4, with SGD lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0 as declared in the request's measured-invocation definition.

Loss semantics (source accumulate()): each microbatch contributes model(input_ids=tokens, labels=tokens, use_cache=False).loss / accumulation_steps and the step loss is the sum of those terms; any other scaling or reduction changes the gradients and violates the reference-fidelity checks.

Deterministic fixtures so independent workers reproduce one reference (source make_model/make_inputs): weights from torch.manual_seed(20261020), token ids from a per-rank torch.Generator seeded 31000+rank; request quality relies on these exact seeded fixtures (assets is empty by design).

Numerical policy from common.configure is required for reference fidelity and frozen by the request (no precision changes): FP32 model, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark False.

Architecture frozen (request: do not change model architecture): GPT-2 124M per workloads.json gpt2_ddp_training.model (n_layer 12, n_embd 768, n_head 12, vocab_size 50257, n_positions 1024) with resid/embd/attn dropout 0.0, use_cache=False, attn_implementation 'eager' (source make_model).

The source's division between setup and timed work is preserved: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is the first statement of the timed accumulate and stays inside run(); reset() must not pre-clear gradients or otherwise move timed work out of the measured invocation.

Real inter-rank gradient synchronization over NCCL must occur inside the measured step (baseline: DDP allreduce on the final microbatch); the required observation communication_kernel_sum_ms is collected by the framework's torch_communication collector in separate diagnostic runs and is not fabricated by the adapter.
Step-time constraint (request objective.constraints): per-repeat max-across-ranks step_ms must remain <= 1.05x the baseline; communication reductions may not be obtained by slowing the clean step.

Observation completeness for a training workload (adapter contract): loss, all gradients and all updated parameters are returned as full detached tensors, and no accuracy or convergence is claimed beyond the source's reference-fidelity checks.
assumptions: Baseline reproduces source implementation choices verbatim for fidelity, not because the task requires them: DDP(broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, device_ids=[local device]), no_sync() on the first accumulation_steps-1 microbatches, and SGD foreach=False. Alternative synchronization schedules or DDP settings that keep the gradient/parameter checks green and respect the step_ms constraint are permissible for optimized variants; this baseline keeps the source's.

The adapter does not reconstruct the rank-0 serial reference, run close_check/negative_check, broadcast gradient replicas, or install the bucket inventory comm hook: the source treats these as correctness/measurement infrastructure, and the framework collects and validates observations and the required communication metrics (request required_observations and objective.source collector).

The gloo control subgroup and before_run() barrier mirror the source's pre-repeat coordination outside the timer; if subgroup creation were unavailable the barrier would be skipped and the framework's own boundary synchronization would apply.

Architecture constants are read from inputs/source/workloads.json (then the request's source_root) when reachable, with an identical embedded fallback; only workload dimensions (world_size, micro_batch, sequence_length, accumulation_steps) come from request['workload'], so a validated workload variant with different values replays unchanged.
request['assets'] is intentionally empty: the source declares seeded synthetic weights and token ids rather than pretrained GPT-2, so no pretrained weights are invented or downloaded.

reset() equals the source's reset() (reload the initial CPU state dict): SGD has no momentum state, the step consumes no RNG, and gradients are re-zeroed inside the timed run, so no additional optimizer/RNG/cache restoration is needed; DDP bucket/reducer internals are intentionally left as the source leaves them across repeats.
observe() returns CPU copies of the loss, every named gradient and every named updated parameter so correctness capture does not inflate peak_allocated_bytes reported by metrics() after the timer.

metrics() exposes the source's clean per-invocation project metrics (step_ms, tokens_per_second, peak_allocated_bytes, plus effective_batch, tokens_per_step and parameter_count from the source record); communication_kernel_sum_ms is not computed inside run()/metrics() because the objective has a source collector descriptor and is measured by the framework in separate diagnostic runs.

warmup=2, repeats=5, continuous_steps=2 and the 3 profiled diagnostic iterations are framework measurement parameters, not adapter work: the adapter performs exactly one accumulated step per run() and supports back-to-back run() calls without reset for the continuous-steps state check.

The held-out workload longer_sequence (world_size 2, micro_batch 1, sequence_length 256, accumulation_steps 2) is a reserved validation config, not part of this frozen request, and is not executed here.

Source CLI/runner behavior (argument parsing, output directories, torchrun launch, result.json writing, metadata/nvidia-smi inventory) is runner infrastructure outside the adapter's measured workload.

understanding.json.completion: One measured invocation is exactly one accumulated DDP training step, matching source step(): optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True), then accumulation_steps forward/backward microbatches of token ids shaped (micro_batch, sequence_length) with the first accumulation_steps-1 under model.no_sync() and the final microbatch running the DDP gradient allreduce through the reducer, each microbatch loss scaled by 1/accumulation_steps and summed; then optimizer.step() with SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False) and torch.cuda.synchronize() inside the timed call. Model construction and weight seeding, DDP wrapping, input generation, the initial state-dict snapshot, reset, the gloo control barrier, correctness checks, gradient-replica broadcast, bucket inventory hooks and the separate communication profiler traces are all outside the measured boundary. The communication objective uses the source's separate completion boundary: a framework diagnostic run that profiles the full step and sums device NCCL kernel durations per rank.
understanding.json.state_protocol: prepare(context, request) reproduces source setup: common.configure numerics (4 CPU threads, manual_seed(20261020), set_device(context['device']), TF32 off for matmul/cudnn, cudnn.benchmark off, float32 matmul precision 'highest'), builds GPT2LMHeadModel on context['device'] from the frozen architecture config, wraps it in DDP(device_ids=[local device], broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True), creates SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False) and the per-rank seeded token inputs, snapshots the initial state dict on CPU, and creates the source's side gloo control group; it uses the worker's existing process group and never initializes another default one. run(state) executes the full step described in completion and returns {'loss', 'microbatch_losses'}; live allocations the source keeps (inputs, initial snapshot, model, optimizer) stay referenced in state. reset(state) reloads the CPU snapshot into the module exactly like source reset(); SGD momentum=0.0 holds no optimizer state and gradients are re-cleared inside the timed accumulate, so no other mutable state exists; the process group is never destroyed. observe(state, result) returns detached CPU tensors: total loss, per-microbatch losses, every named gradient and every post-update named parameter (None only where a gradient is genuinely absent). metrics(state, result, elapsed_ms) returns finite native-unit project metrics (step_ms, loss, tokens_per_step, tokens_per_second, effective_batch, parameter_count, peak_allocated_bytes) with tokens_per_second derived from the unchanged work amount; the communication objective is measured by the framework's torch_communication collector in separate profiled diagnostic runs, so no communication value is fabricated here. models(state) exposes the DDP-wrapped module as {'model': DDP} for discovery and controlled replacement. set_mode(state, mode) records quality/measure/profile with no behavioral change: the identical full step runs in every mode because observations are captured after the same timed work. before_run(state) performs the source's gloo control-group barrier (falling back to the default group barrier if the side group could not be created) outside the timer.
invariants: Numerical policy frozen as source common.configure: FP32 model, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark off, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'); the framework re-checks these policies around run.

Deterministic fixtures: torch.manual_seed(20261020) immediately before GPT2LMHeadModel construction (identical initial weights on every rank), token ids from torch.Generator().manual_seed(31000 + rank); assets are empty by design and no pretrained weights or downloads are involved.

Architecture frozen: GPT2Config(n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024, resid_pdrop=0.0, embd_pdrop=0.0, attn_pdrop=0.0, use_cache=False, attn_implementation='eager'), module kept in train() mode with .float() weights.

DDP wrapper frozen as source: device_ids=[context local device], broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True; the adapter installs no communication hook and no automatic optimization target.

Accumulation semantics frozen: first accumulation_steps-1 microbatches under model.no_sync(), the final microbatch triggers the DDP gradient allreduce; per-microbatch loss is model(input_ids=tokens, labels=tokens, use_cache=False).loss / accumulation_steps and the step loss is their sum.

Optimizer frozen: torch.optim.SGD(module.parameters(), lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False); optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) stays inside the timed invocation exactly as in source accumulate(), never pre-cleared in reset().

Work amount frozen per request['workload'] (world_size=2, micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4 -> effective batch 8, 1024 tokens per step); dimensions and counts are read from request['workload'] in prepare(), not embedded as constants, so a validated variant reuses this adapter.

reset(state) restores the initial CPU state dict before every measured invocation; timed step ends with torch.cuda.synchronize() as in source step(); step time is the per-rank local wall time aggregated by the framework (max across ranks), with control barriers excluded.

Correctness scope is source reference fidelity only: rank-0 serial no-DDP accumulation of the same global batch compared with grad/parameter tolerances, plus bit-exact cross-rank gradient replicas; observe() therefore exposes the full loss, all gradients and all updated parameters, and no accuracy or convergence claim is made.

Objective semantics frozen: communication_kernel_sum_ms is the per-rank sum of device NCCL kernel durations over the full step (includes device waiting, not wire/critical-path time), aggregated max across ranks then median over the profiled repeats, collected by the framework's torch_communication collector in separate diagnostic runs under the step_ms <= 1.05x baseline constraint.
assumptions: The worker has already bound CUDA and initialized the NCCL process group; the adapter only uses context['device'] (never a hardcoded physical GPU) and creates the source's side gloo control group via dist.new_group for pre-step barriers, destroying nothing.

inputs/source/workloads.json ships next to the adapter and is read for the frozen GPT-2 architecture dims; if it is absent, identical frozen fallback dims (n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024) are used. Workload dimensions always come from request['workload'].

SGD momentum=0.0 means the optimizer holds no state between steps, so reloading the initial module state dict is a complete reset, exactly matching source reset(); DDP reducer carries no cross-step numerics.

Gradients remain valid after optimizer.step() until the next invocation's zero_grad, so observe() run immediately after run() sees the averaged gradients and post-update parameters; observations are detached CPU clones so later resets cannot alias them.

The framework collects communication_kernel_sum_ms via its torch_communication collector in separate diagnostic runs, performs cross-rank gradient-replica validation and passive bucket inventory itself; the adapter reports no communication value and installs no hook, so those are not missing task semantics.

Framework measurement fields (warmup=2, repeats=5, continuous_steps=2) are infrastructure: one run() is one accumulated step, and consecutive continuous steps run back-to-back with reset only before the sequence, which the stateless-after-reset design reproduces.
The source's held-out workload 'longer_sequence' (sequence_length=256, accumulation_steps=2) is a reserved validation configuration, not part of this frozen request, and is not executed.

set_mode('quality'/'measure'/'profile') does not alter execution or work amount: the source has no separate correctness-capture path, so full gradients and parameters are observable after the identical timed step in every mode.
